title: Book One · Chapter 145: Nine Candles
story:
Ronan is nine on a Sunday. Mum makes his favourite breakfast. Dad puts a little round cake on the table after lunch. There are no candles on it. He draws nine candles on a piece of paper. He stands the paper beside the plate.

“These last longer,” he says.

“I cannot blow them out.”

Dad leans forward and blows. The whole paper falls over. Mum quickly lifts the cake out of the way.

Ronan laughs so hard he forgets to make a wish. He makes it quietly while Mum cuts three pieces. He does not ask for the old red bike. He wants a bicycle of his own. It must be big enough for his longer legs.

After lunch Dad brings Ronan's money box from the shelf. Ronan opens it himself. The coins make a small heap. There are folded notes from birthdays too. He saved money. He did not spend it. He kept a list as well. But two old numbers are hard to read.

They count slowly. Mum counts the coins, then checks his list. One coin has rolled under Dad's sleeve. He lifts his arm slowly. He points to the hiding coin.

“A late guest.”

They count it in. Ronan writes the total on a clean sheet. It is more than last year, but not enough for every bicycle in every shop.

Dad and Mum have talked about his birthday gift. They can add some money for the bicycle. They choose to give him this money. They have kept it apart from rent, food, and Mum's work money for new cloth.

“We can look for a good used bike,” Dad says. “Plain. The right size. It may take time.”

“Not today?”

“Today we count. Another day we look.”

Ronan touches the old bell on his shelf. It is cool in his hand. He kept it when the red bike was sold. There is a little mark on its side. He rubs the mark with his thumb. He has touched that same place many times.

“Can this go on it?”

“If it fits safely,” Dad says. “We will check.”

Mum makes two columns on the sheet. One is Ronan's money. The other is their birthday part. She puts the possible spending limit below them. They must not spend more than this amount. They have not seen a bicycle they want yet.

Ronan puts the coins back in the box himself. Mum keeps their birthday part in a separate envelope. They put the clean money sheet on the shelf. All three can find it there. No one asks him to do extra work for it. This money is for his birthday. It is not pay for the school display.

Leo comes in the afternoon with a small paper cover for the street-game cards. He made it himself. One side is crooked. The cards fit anyway.

“Nine is better than eight,” he says.

“You said that about eight.”

“I was right then too.”

They eat the last two small pieces of cake. “Do you have a bike now?” Leo asks. Ronan shakes his head.

“A plan for one.”

“Can I see it?”

Ronan shows him the money sheet, not the money. Leo looks at the two columns and nods. Then they go outside with the ball. The street day is three weeks away. A bicycle may come after that, if they find the right one. Today he is nine and the cake is gone. He turns quickly when Leo runs after him. Leo still cannot catch him on the first turn.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：used＝二手的；spending limit＝支出上限；columns＝表格的两栏。

情节提示：candles＝蜡烛；notes＝这里指纸币；rent＝房租。

理解：1. 买自行车的预算由哪两部分组成？2. 为什么生日当天还没有买车？
